clue.text: Monkeys with dirty child not right wearing hats

indicators.note: the hats are worn around the child, so the child's letters sit inside

parts.note: caps are hats

indicators.note: not right means the R for right is taken away

parts.note: an urchin is a grubby, scruffy child

explanation.surface: A troop of monkeys accompanied by a grubby youngster in hats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not right' looks like a description of the child's behaviour, but it tells you to drop a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Capuchins are a genus of small South American primates named for their hooded look.

clue.text: Joe in US chasing my dog

indicators.note: chasing means coming behind, so this piece follows the exclamation

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
GI Joe is the American private soldier

explanation.surface: An American soldier runs after somebody's dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The corgi is a short-legged Welsh breed, so it is an example of a dog.

clue.text: Smooth, like well-oiled locks

parts.note: locks are hair here, not door fittings, slicked with a scented hair ointment

explanation.walkthrough: Well-oiled locks suggest door locks that turn smoothly; the locks are hair dressed with oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomade is a perfumed hair ointment, so hair dressed with it is sleek and glossy.

clue.text: Could it be grandfather, white-headed — I'm blown away!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a timepiece, a grandfather being a tall case one
second meaning: the fluffy white seed head of a dandelion, blown away in the children's game

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation reads like an amazed old man; children blow the white seed head of a dandelion to 'tell the time'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a timepiece, of which a grandfather is a type, and a dandelion's round seed head.

clue.text: Religious doctor claims one should get injected

indicators.note: the one is pushed into the rearranged letters like a needle
to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A medic insists a patient needs an injection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the medic but is the anagram signal on CLAIMS, with I put in.
explanation.definitionFit: Islamic describes things belonging to Islam, so it is a particular religious adjective.

clue.text: Dropping the lot after club's last game

indicators.note: this piece comes after the letter from club

parts.note: a stool is a dropping, faeces

indicators.note: the last of the club is its final letter

parts.note: last letter of club
all means the lot, everything

explanation.surface: Losing everything after the final stage of a club's match.
explanation.walkthrough: Stoolball is an old English bat-and-ball game, a forerunner of cricket, still played in Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoolball is a team bat-and-ball game, so it is an example of a game.

clue.text: Leader avoiding fresh hazard

indicators.note: the word loses its leader, its first letter, which is avoided

parts.note: a brisk wind is a fresh one

explanation.surface: A chief who keeps clear of a new danger.
explanation.walkthrough: BRISK without its first letter B.
explanation.definitionFit: A risk is a danger or peril, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Proves false and won't take son out for tea, we're told

indicators.note: the son goes out and the tea comes in his place

parts.note: refuses means won't take

indicators.note: we're told means heard, so the drink stands for the letter that sounds like it

parts.note: the drink tea, spoken, is the letter T

explanation.surface: Someone shows a claim is untrue and declines to take a son out for tea.
explanation.walkthrough: The second S of REFUSES is replaced by T, the letter that sounds like tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To refute an argument is to show that it is wrong, so the verb means proves false.

clue.text: Startled schoolmaster forced to speak

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the two words run together into the answer

parts.note: sir is a pupil's name for a schoolmaster and prised means forced open

explanation.surface: A shocked teacher is made to say something.
explanation.walkthrough: SIR PRISED, spoken, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be surprised is to be taken aback or shocked, which is what startled means.

clue.text: Percussionist's effect is diverting, full of spirit

indicators.note: the amusing word is filled with the drink, so it goes inside

parts.note: droll means amusing, diverting
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A drummer's flourish is amusing and lively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' suggests liveliness in the surface, but it is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum roll is the rapid continuous beating a percussionist produces for suspense.

clue.text: Steer, following ring road to reach city

parts.note: a steer is a bullock, an ox
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Driving by the ring road to get into town.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford is an English university city, so it is an example of a city.

clue.text: Small ruminant or two going west

definitions.text: Small ruminant or two going west

indicators.note: in an across answer west is leftwards, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a kid is a young goat, a small cud-chewer
a second of them, so the young goat appears twice

explanation.surface: A little grazing animal, or a couple of them, heading off westwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Two KIDs side by side, written backwards, give the antelope, itself a small ruminant, so the whole clue is both definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The dik-dik is a tiny African antelope, and antelopes chew the cud.

clue.text: Landed on island, in custody of Catholic queen's army

indicators.note: held by the queen, so these letters go inside her name

parts.note: Mary I of England was the Catholic queen

indicators.note: in an across answer, on means placed after, so landed comes after island

parts.note: lit means landed or alighted, as a bird lit on a branch

explanation.surface: Someone came ashore on an island and was taken prisoner by a Catholic monarch's soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Catholic queen is Mary I of England, daughter of Henry VIII.
explanation.definitionFit: The military as a noun means the armed forces collectively, the soldiery.

clue.text: Familiar with international being dropped off outside ground

indicators.note: the international is let off and leaves the word outside
ground means crushed and broken up, so the remaining letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A foreign player is left at the edge of a stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: OUTSIDE without I leaves OUTSDE, which is rearranged. 'Ground' looks like a sports ground but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To be used to something is to be accustomed to it, an idiom for familiarity.

clue.text: Outsiders to stage child's play, a blow for Brighton?

indicators.note: the outsiders of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of stage
something easy is child's play, a breeze

explanation.surface: The edges of a stage, a simple show, and a gust on the south coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighton is an English seaside resort; the blow is a wind, not a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea breeze is a wind off the sea, the sort expected at a seaside town.

clue.text: Jesse's father forced niece's submission

parts.note: in the Bible Obed was the father of Jesse, King David's father

indicators.note: forced means wrenched out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word niece, with 's as a link meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: A patriarch bullies his niece into giving in.
explanation.walkthrough: Obed, son of Ruth and Boaz, is a biblical figure; the 's after niece reads as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Obedience is compliance with orders, the act of yielding or submitting to authority.

clue.text: Most vulgar broadcast coverage of the Oscars

indicators.note: broadcast as scattered, so the letters are spread about
the covering of a word is its outer letters

parts.note: first and last letters of the

explanation.surface: The crudest televised reporting of the Academy Awards.
explanation.walkthrough: TE (the outside of 'the') joins OSCARS and the eight letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse means crude or rude, so the superlative is a synonym for the most vulgar.

clue.text: I'm going to manage in style

parts.note: to fare is to get on, manage
well can mean in style or properly, as in living well

explanation.surface: Someone announcing they will cope with panache.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the words a departing person says.
explanation.definitionFit: Farewell is a parting word, said when leaving, so it stands for an announcement of departure.

clue.text: Passes England's opener, run out close to stumps

indicators.note: a word's opener is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of England's
to lapse is to run out or expire

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

parts.note: last letter of stumps

explanation.surface: England's opening batsman is run out just before the end of play.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket words are scenery: stumps is the close of a day's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that elapses passes or goes by, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Patchy skin condition spreading into leg

indicators.note: the letters spread out and reform in a new order

explanation.surface: A rash creeping into someone's leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Lentigo is a medical term for a small brown spot on the skin, a freckle-like patch.

clue.text: University in country area yielding capital in Africa

indicators.note: the university sits inside the country

parts.note: a land is a country

explanation.surface: A college set in rural land produces an African capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: U sits in LAND, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Luanda is the capital city of Angola, on Africa's Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Country fair Jack missed in song

indicators.note: these letters go inside the song

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera

indicators.note: Jack is missing, so its letter is taken away

parts.note: just means fair
J is the abbreviation for jack, as in cards

explanation.surface: A national fair where Jack was absent from the singing.
explanation.walkthrough: JUST without J leaves UST, which goes into ARIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria is a nation in central Europe, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Making response, Charlie moves to the front

indicators.note: the letter for Charlie is shifted from its place up to the start

parts.note: a reaction is a response
C is Charlie in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A reply in which someone called Charlie steps forward.
explanation.walkthrough: The C in the middle of REACTION is lifted to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Creation is the act of making or producing something, as a noun synonym.

clue.text: Post a second notice

parts.note: a sign is a notice put up

explanation.surface: Put up one more notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like putting up a notice, but it means appoint to a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To post someone somewhere is to assign or appoint them to that station.

clue.text: Generous porter letting politician in

indicators.note: letting together with the closing in says the beer admits the politician
with letting, says the politician is let inside the beer

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A kindly doorman admits a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' looks like the doorman but is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means plentiful or more than enough, as a generous helping is.

clue.text: Grand people's prayer

parts.note: G is the slang abbreviation for a grand, a thousand
a race is a people

explanation.surface: A grand family's devotions.
explanation.definitionFit: Grace is the short prayer of thanks said before a meal.

clue.text: Famous disabled London columnist?

parts.note: the admiral lost an arm and an eye, and his statue stands on a column in Trafalgar Square

explanation.walkthrough: 'Columnist' suggests a newspaper writer; here it is someone standing on top of a column.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio Nelson, the one-armed admiral, tops Nelson's Column in central London.

clue.text: Army's initial breaches endanger sovereign

indicators.note: the letter breaks into the word, so it goes inside

parts.note: to imperil is to endanger

indicators.note: the initial of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of Army's

explanation.surface: An invading force's leading attack threatens a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside IMPERIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperial means relating to an emperor, and so having supreme royal authority, as an adjective.

clue.text: Stephen Spender's caged birds

indicators.note: the answer is shut inside the poet's name, as birds in a cage

explanation.surface: The poet Stephen Spender kept birds in cages.
explanation.walkthrough: Stephen Spender was an English poet; the letters run across his two names.
explanation.definitionFit: Hens are female birds, especially domestic fowl, so they are an example of birds.

clue.text: Clear Devon waters hosting unique rodent

indicators.note: the river plays host, holding the other letters within it

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, in south-west England
one can mean unique, the only one
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: Devon's rivers are free of a rare rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear' looks like a description of clean water, but it is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate is to clear someone of blame, a verb synonym.
